one_liner: Checks that a company's accounts are true, and works out what it owes.
job_roles: Audit Assistant | Statutory Auditor | Internal Auditor | Tax Consultant | GST Practitioner | Forensic Auditor | Financial Reporting Analyst | Transfer Pricing Analyst
industrial_sectors: BFSI | MEPSC | IT-ITES | RASCI | CGSC | EXT-GOVT
licensing_body: Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI)
self_emp_route: Own practice after ICAI membership — audit, tax and advisory for small and mid-sized businesses. The most common destination in the profession, and it needs a certificate of practice, not capital.
ai_reason: Reconciliation, ledger scrutiny and return preparation are heavily exposed and already automating. What protects the profession is that the SIGNATURE carries statutory liability — an audit opinion is a person taking legal responsibility, which software cannot do.
role_spread: [Forensic Auditor, Internal Auditor] higher: reasoning, openness, dogmatism / lower: agreeableness
path_to_entry: class_12: ANY stream — commerce, science or arts all qualify for CA Foundation -> foundation: CA Foundation; graduates with the required percentage skip it and enter Intermediate directly -> intermediate: CA Intermediate, two groups -> articleship: THREE YEARS of articleship training under a practising CA — this is the qualification, not an internship -> final: CA Final plus the mandatory AICITSS course, then ICAI membership
review_reason: COST & MANAGEMENT ACCOUNTANT (ICMAI) is not listed as a separate profession. ICMAI is a statutory body under the Cost and Works Accountants Act 1959 with its own three-stage route, so it arguably deserves its own record; it is currently absent rather than merged. Verify the ICMAI route and decide.
nuances: [class12_prerequisite] CA is open after class 12 from ANY stream, including arts. It is one of the very few high-earning Indian professions with no subject gate at all, and it does not require a degree — a fact frequently missed by students who assume commerce is compulsory. || [years_to_qualify] The three-year articleship is part of the qualification, not experience after it. That is why the realistic time is about five years and why the pass rate, not the admission, is the real filter.

one_liner: Keeps the books straight — entries, invoices, GST and payroll.
job_roles: Accounts Assistant | Bookkeeper | Accounts Payable Executive | Accounts Receivable Executive | Payroll Executive | GST Return Preparer | Billing Executive | Debt Recovery Agent | Collections Officer
industrial_sectors: BFSI | MEPSC | RASCI | IT-ITES | FICSI | LSC
self_emp_route: Independent bookkeeping and GST filing practice serving several small businesses — very low capital, built on local relationships.
ai_reason: THE MOST EXPOSED PROFESSION IN THIS SECTOR. Data entry, reconciliation, invoice matching and return preparation are exactly what automation does best, and accounting software is absorbing them fast. The client relationship at the small-business end is what remains.
path_to_entry: class_12: Commerce is usual but not required -> certificate: Tally, Zoho Books or a similar accounting package — this is what employers screen on -> degree: A B.Com helps and is common, but is not the gate -> employment: Every business of any size, plus accounting and outsourcing firms
review_reason: SITS EXACTLY ON THE FILTER BOUNDARY, and survives by rounding. Mid-career midpoint is 6.0 and AI exposure is high at 75 — the compensation rule cuts a profession below 6.0 with high exposure, so a tenth of a lakh either way decides whether this ships. It is also the most AI-exposed record in Sector 6 and one of the largest entry-level employers of commerce graduates in India. Two decisions: whether the band is right, and whether a profession this exposed should be recommended as a destination or only as a route into Chartered Accountancy.
nuances: [professional_sector] The base layer of finance, listed beside Chartered Accountant at the apex on the same principle as Mason beside Civil Engineer. It is also the most realistic formal-sector entry point in finance for a student without the time or money for a five-year professional qualification.

one_liner: Works out what a company or an investment is really worth.
job_roles: Financial Analyst | FP&A Analyst | Equity Research Associate | Credit Analyst | Investment Banking Analyst | Valuation Analyst | Corporate Finance Analyst
entrance_exams: CAT | XAT | CMAT | CUET (BBA/B.Com) | NMAT | SNAP | IIFT
self_emp_route: Independent valuation or advisory practice, usually after years in a firm and often alongside a CA qualification.
ai_reason: Model building, comparables and report drafting are directly exposed and already assisted. Judging whether a forecast is credible, and defending a valuation to a committee, are not.
role_spread: [Investment Banking Analyst] higher: conscientiousness, attention_span, emotional_stability / lower: -
path_to_entry: class_12: Any stream; commerce and science are common -> degree: Any bachelor's — B.Com, BBA, economics and engineering all feed in -> certification: CFA, FRM or an MBA in finance is the usual differentiator -> employment: Banks, investment firms, rating agencies, corporate finance teams, global capability centres

one_liner: Works inside a bank — lending, deposits, and looking after customers' money.
job_roles: Probationary Officer | Relationship Manager | Credit Officer | Branch Operations Officer | Loan Processing Officer | Treasury Analyst | Trade Finance Officer
entrance_exams: IBPS PO / Clerk | SBI PO / Clerk | RBI Grade B | NABARD Grade A
ai_reason: Transaction processing, document verification and routine credit scoring are heavily exposed, and branch banking is shrinking as a result. Relationship and credit judgment roles survive better than operations ones.
path_to_entry: class_12: Any stream -> degree: Any bachelor's in any discipline -> exam: IBPS PO or SBI PO for public sector banks; private banks hire directly and through campus -> employment: Public sector banks, private banks, small finance banks, NBFCs
nuances: [entrance_exams] Public sector bank recruitment is one of the few well-paid formal careers in India reachable with a degree in ANY subject and no prior experience, decided entirely by a written examination. For a student from a non-elite college it is often the most realistic high-value entry route that exists.

one_liner: Prices risk, and decides what a claim is really worth.
job_roles: Underwriter | Claims Assessor | Insurance Surveyor & Loss Assessor | Medical Coder | Medical Biller | Claims Analyst (health) | Risk Analyst (insurance) | Bancassurance Officer
self_emp_route: Licensed insurance broking or a surveyor and loss assessor practice, both of which need IRDAI licensing.
ai_reason: Coding, billing and routine claims adjudication are among the most automatable work in the dataset. Loss assessment in the field and underwriting a non-standard risk are not.
role_spread: [Medical Coder, Medical Biller, Claims Analyst (health)] higher: attention_span, conscientiousness / lower: extraversion, reasoning
path_to_entry: class_12: Any stream -> degree: Any bachelor's; life sciences graduates are preferred for health claims and coding -> certification: IRDAI licensing for agents and surveyors; CPC or CCS certification for medical coding -> employment: Insurers, third-party administrators, brokers, healthcare BPOs
nuances: [job_roles] The medical coding and billing roles were routed here from Sector 4. Classifying documents against a published rulebook to get a payer to pay is claims work; the documents being medical is the industry, which is why HSSC is a tag here rather than the sector. || [ai_exposure] The coding and billing roles are far more exposed than the profession's overall score, and they are also its largest employers by headcount. A student entering through that door should be told they are at the exposed end.

one_liner: Manages other people's money and advises them where to put it.
job_roles: Wealth Manager | Investment Advisor | Mutual Fund Distributor | Portfolio Analyst | Financial Planner | Private Banking Associate
self_emp_route: Independent financial advisory practice, which needs SEBI registration and NISM certification rather than capital. Income moves with assets under advice.
ai_reason: Portfolio construction and rebalancing are exactly what robo-advisory does, and product selection is commoditising. Persuading someone not to sell in a crash is the part that has kept this profession human.
path_to_entry: class_12: Any stream -> degree: Any bachelor's -> certification: NISM certification is mandatory to advise or distribute; CFP and CFA are the differentiators -> employment: Wealth management arms of banks, brokerages, independent advisory firms

one_liner: Uses mathematics to price risk decades into the future.
job_roles: Actuarial Analyst | Pricing Actuary | Reserving Actuary | Valuation Actuary | Actuarial Consultant | Risk Modelling Analyst
self_emp_route: Independent actuarial consulting after qualification, typically to smaller insurers and pension schemes.
ai_reason: Heavily quantitative but built on foundational mathematics rather than retrievable knowledge, and the output is a professional judgment an insurer relies on. Model automation assists it rather than replacing it.
path_to_entry: class_12: Strong mathematics is effectively required even where it is not formally mandated -> entrance: ACET, the Institute of Actuaries of India entrance test -> exams: A long series of professional examinations taken while working — most candidates take many years -> employment: Life and general insurers, reinsurers, consulting firms, pension advisers
nuances: [years_to_qualify] Seven years is the realistic figure and it may be optimistic. The professional examinations have low pass rates and are taken alongside full-time work, so many candidates take a decade and a substantial number never complete them. Anyone considering this should treat the exam sequence, not the entrance test, as the real gate. || [licensing_body] The Actuaries Act 2006 does not merely regulate the title — its DEFINITION of an actuary includes being a fellow member of the Institute of Actuaries of India. You cannot be an actuary in Indian law without IAI fellowship, which makes this one of the hardest statutory gates in the taxonomy.

one_liner: Studies how money, work and policy move through a whole economy.
job_roles: Economist | Research Economist | Policy Economist | Macroeconomic Analyst | Development Economist | Econometrician
entrance_exams: CUET (BA/B.Sc Economics) | DSE / ISI / JNU entrance (MA) | RBI Grade B (DEPR) | Indian Economic Service (UPSC)
self_emp_route: Independent research and policy consulting to think tanks, industry bodies and international agencies.
ai_reason: Data work and literature summarising are exposed. Framing an economic question and defending a policy judgment in public are not — the clarity and foundational-knowledge shares carry it.
path_to_entry: class_12: Any stream; mathematics is a strong advantage and required by some programmes -> degree: BA or B.Sc Economics -> post_graduate: MA or M.Sc Economics is the real entry qualification; DSE, ISI, JNU and IGIDR are the recognised routes -> employment: RBI and government, banks and rating agencies, think tanks, international organisations
nuances: [professional_sector] Routed here from Sector 3 Science & Research. Economics is empirical, but its object of concern is money and value, and it has its own professional sector. Research method alone does not decide the sector when a sector exists for the subject itself. || [mid_stream_entry] Corrected from restart_undergrad. An MA or M.Sc Economics does not require a bachelor's in economics — engineering, mathematics, statistics and commerce graduates enter routinely, and several of the strongest Indian programmes prefer a mathematical background over an economics one. The subject gate is mathematics ability, not a prior economics degree.
